persona.bio: Jess, 29, event coordinator at a restaurant group in Chicago. Her Gmail inbox is full of clients, caterers, florists and AV people. She keeps the run of show, floor plans and vendor timelines in Google Sheets, collects headcounts and dietary lists the week before each event, and is on site with a headset on event nights. Vendor follow ups eat her afternoons, and she loses track of who hasn't replied. She uses ChatGPT a few times a week for emails. Her company is fine with AI and IT said she can connect ChatGPT to her work Gmail.

path.role: You’re an event coordinator for a restaurant group in Chicago, planning private events and running them on the night.

steps.note: I coordinate private events for a restaurant group in Chicago. I plan them with clients and run them on the night. I write to vendors, clients and my own team. My tone is warm, direct and professional, never stiff. I keep messages short, usually two to four sentences, with one clear ask and a clear deadline. Never add details I did not give you, like times, prices, headcounts or menu items. If something is missing, put it in square brackets so I can fill it in. Never invent a reason or a promise on my behalf. Give me a draft I can read and change before anything goes out.

steps.title: Your vendor follow ups, drafted from your inbox for your OK
steps.read: Your vendor follow ups now start from your Gmail, not your memory. ChatGPT drafts each follow up and waits for your OK before anything goes out. That suits your job, because vendors who go quiet can hold up a floor plan or a load in time. You read every draft and you choose what to send.

material.label: Instructions for your assistant
items: I am an event coordinator for a restaurant group in Chicago. I plan private events and run them on the night. Look through my Gmail for emails I sent to vendors, like AV, florists, rentals and music, where I asked a question or for a confirmation and have not had a reply. Count an email as waiting if it has a clear ask and no answer yet. Wait two business days before a first nudge and another two business days before a second one. If the email mentions a deadline, like needing something locked by a certain day, mention it in the nudge. Write the way I do: warm, short, direct, one clear ask, two to four sentences. Do not add details I did not give you. Use square brackets for anything missing. Draft each follow up in the chat, tell me who it is for and which email it is about, and never send anything. Give back a short list of who is still waiting at the end.

material.label: Your follow up wording
items: Hi [first name], following up on [the item] for the [date] event. Can you confirm [what you need] by [day]? I need it settled for [what depends on it]. Thank you!

Hi [first name], checking in again on [the item] for [date]. I still need your confirmation on [what you need] by [day] so I can finalize [what depends on it]. If something changed, please let me know and we will work around it. Thanks, [your name]

steps.title: Your client texts, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your common client replies now live on your phone’s keyboard. Each one is a few letters away, so you stop retyping the same message many times a day. You change a name or a time and send. That keeps your answers steady, even while you are on your feet on an event night.

material.label: Your common replies
items: Hi [first name], thank you for reaching out about your event! I would love to help. Could you tell me your date, guest count and the kind of event you have in mind?
Hi [first name], thanks for your patience. I am checking on that and will get back to you by [day].
Hi [first name], your date of [date] is confirmed. I will send the next details shortly.
Hi [first name], I can send over our event options. What is the best email to reach you?
Hi [first name], just checking in. Could you confirm [what you need] by [day]? That lets me keep everything on track for your event.
Hi [first name], we are all set for [date]. I will be there on the night. If anything changes before then, text me here.
Thank you so much for celebrating with us, [first name]! It was a pleasure hosting you.

safeUse: Never type a client’s full name, phone number, email or home address into ChatGPT. Use square brackets instead.
Keep payment details, card numbers and contract amounts out of the chat.
Leave out guests’ allergy and health details tied to a name.
Do not paste vendor contact details or private account information.
Read every draft before it goes out, and check dates, times and counts against your own records.
steps.askMessage: Hi [manager’s name], I would like to use ChatGPT to help with my day to day work as an event coordinator. I have in mind drafting vendor follow ups from my Gmail, keeping vendor schedules organized, writing client texts and emails, and making event lists. Which AI tools are approved for work, and what am I allowed to use them for? I also want to know if I may connect my work email, since I would read and approve every draft before it is sent. Please let me know so I can set this up the right way.

design.today: You chase vendor follow ups many times a day, often from a mental list. Gmail labels are a mess, so you mostly remember who still owes you an answer.
design.newWay: Once a week, a read-only task checks your Gmail and gives you a list of vendors who have not answered. For the ones you decide to chase, your chat tool drafts the follow up in your voice, using the details from the original thread like the load-in time and the Friday deadline. You read each draft and send it yourself. The list replaces the mental note, so nothing slips on a busy event week.

steps.goal: Get ChatGPT ready on your phone and computer so the same setup works wherever you are.
Save a short note about your role, your tone with vendors and how you sign off, so every draft sounds like you.
Set up a weekly list of vendors who have not answered your emails, read from Gmail only.
Have your chat tool draft follow ups from the Gmail threads you pick, asking before it sends anything.
Pick the three or four follow up situations you write most, like confirming a time, a missing quote or a late delivery, and note the details each one needs.
